title: Norvant explainer launch kit: trim the master from one long take, pull six mixed-light poster frames to one house look, vectorize the wordmark, and data-merge the typeset title / lower-third / end cards
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com motion-graphics brief (a client with raw explainer footage, a logo, colour references and a loose outline, wanting a clear informative cut plus on-brand text overlays — lower-thirds, call-outs, title and end cards — and the linked assets organised for future tweaks). Laundered to a fictional workflow-automation company, 'Norvant' (a hexring glyph + a slate-and-amber wordmark) — no real company, product, person, or trademark is named; Freelancer.com is only the sourcing platform. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the headless connector cannot composite typeset text onto a moving video, cannot trim to timecode, cannot do motion graphics, and video_create_quick_cut can only SHORTEN ONE supplied clip (it cannot assemble multiple clips into a master or lengthen one) — so those parts of the original brief are honestly re-cast to what the connectors genuinely produce. The VIDEO lane works from ONE long primary source: a single continuous ~3.5-minute (~210s) UHD interview take shot in one sitting as the room light was deliberately changed through the session (warm tungsten open, cool daylight once the blinds are opened, a golden-hour rake at the close), with an 18% grey card and white chip clipped to the desk edge for the whole take. From that ONE take the async tools deliver only what they actually make: a speech-cleaned, quick-cut ~90-second highlight master (the source take is longer than the cut — a shorten, never an assembly or a lengthen) and a same-length 9:16 reframe downscaled from the UHD-scale master (never upscaled). The real designed work moves to two connector-legal lanes the brief already implies: (1) the on-brand 'overlay' graphics become REAL InDesign-typeset launch cards (title card, two lower-thirds, a stat call-out, a section divider, an end card) produced by a genuine one-file-per-row data-merge of a hand-authored single-record .indd template against a client-supplied copy CSV, each card placing a matched poster frame and the vectorized wordmark — this is the connector-correct way to typeset on-brand text over an image, and it is the artifact the motion designer works from; (2) the 'colour references / colour correction' intent becomes a cross-asset grade: six poster frames pulled via video_render_frame from six moments of the ONE take, spanning its three evolving lighting states, must be neutralised to ONE house white point read off the in-frame grey card so the launch kit reads as one piece. No generative AI, no compositing of image over image, no upscaling, no text-to-image, no video-text compositing, no trim-to-timecode, no multi-clip assembly, no per-artboard export, no image column in a text-only merge, no convert_pdf_to_indd merge target; image placement happens only inside the authored .indd merge.
one_line_ask: Clean the interview audio, trim one long ~3.5-minute interview take DOWN to a 90-second explainer highlight and a same-length 9:16 reframe (never lengthening or assembling), pull six poster frames from that one take at moments spanning its three evolving lighting states and grade them all to one house white point read off the in-frame grey card (keeping intentional warmth where the light itself was warm), prep-and-vectorize the scanned Norvant wordmark, then data-merge the client's authored single-record InDesign card template so every launch card — title, lower-thirds, stat call-out, divider, end card — is typeset and placed as one press-ready page per row.
full_brief:
Norvant is launching a 90-second informative explainer about our workflow-automation platform and we need the whole launch kit built from the raw material we're sending. Here is what you get and what we need back.

Raw material: ONE long continuous UHD recording — about three and a half minutes, shot in a single sitting of our founder talking to camera at her desk with a laptop showing our dashboard. We shot it as one take on purpose and let the room light change through the session: it opens under our warm desk tungsten, we opened the blinds to cool daylight partway through for the dashboard talk, and by the end the low golden-hour sun was raking warm across the desk. So the same take carries a few different looks depending on where you pull from it. On the edge of the desk we clipped a neutral 18% grey card and a small white chip, in frame for the whole take, so the stills can be balanced honestly after the fact. The audio has some steady room hiss. You also get our wordmark, which unfortunately only exists as a slightly crooked desktop scan on off-white paper, a loose narrative outline, and a short CSV of the exact on-screen copy for our launch cards (headlines, the two lower-third names/roles, the call-out stat, the end-card call to action) — bind that copy verbatim, do not rewrite it.

VIDEO: from that one recording we need three things. First, clean the room hiss off the audio. Second, give us a punchy ~90-second highlight cut of the take that surfaces the key points — it's a highlight pulled from the longer recording, not something stitched together or stretched out. Third, give us a same-length 9:16 vertical version for social — same length as the highlight, no trimming. We're not asking for burned-in captions or motion graphics — just the clean cut and the vertical.

POSTER FRAMES — the heart of the colour job: pull six stills from the take to use as the imagery in the launch cards — one hero moment for the title card, two moments for the lower-thirds, one for the stat call-out, one for the section divider, one for the end card. Because the light shifted across the take, straight out of the recording these six stills do NOT match — some read warm, some cool, one is a genuinely golden close. We need all six to look like ONE piece, one house look, as if they were the same shot: balance each one honestly using the grey card we clipped in frame so they share one neutral white point, floor the darks at one shared level (deep but never crushed to solid black), and carry the same appetising, slightly filmic tonality across all six — lifted shadows, protected highlights, a little clarity. They need to read as one continuous set, not six separately-tweaked stills. One thing we care about: where a moment is genuinely warm because the light really was that warm, that mood is intentional — keep the natural life in it, don't drain it grey. On the hero title-card frame, lift the founder off the background so she reads cleanly with room on one side for the headline. When you're done, tell us the white-balance and exposure you landed on for each of the six frames so we can confirm the set is matched.

WORDMARK: get our scanned wordmark clean and razor-sharp as vector art for the cards — it must not look like a fuzzy, crooked scan when it prints.

LAUNCH CARDS: we've hand-built the InDesign card template with the real placeholder fields and an image slot, and we're giving you the copy CSV. Merge them so every launch card — title, the two lower-thirds, the stat call-out, the section divider, the end card — comes out as its own finished page with its copy set in type, its matched poster frame placed, and the vector wordmark in the corner. Hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI PDF, one card per row, plus the six matched frames and the vector logo, all organised so we can tweak later. Acceptance: interview audio noticeably cleaner; a ~90s highlight and a same-length 9:16; every grey card neutral at one shared white point with the darks floored at one shared level; the intentional warmth of the naturally-warm moments kept; the wordmark a crisp skew-free vector; and exactly one finished card per CSV row. Two rounds of feedback should be plenty.

inputs.name: norvant_interview_master_take.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: UHD 3840x2160 raw documentary interview clip, one continuous ~3.5-minute (~210 second) locked-off take: a mid-30s woman founder with dark shoulder-length wavy hair in a rust-brown button-up, seated at a walnut desk in a modern minimalist office with an open laptop showing a plain unbranded workflow dashboard, a brass desk lamp and a ceramic mug on the desk. She talks warmly to camera in a medium shot, gesturing, occasionally leaning toward the laptop to reference the dashboard. Crucially the room light is deliberately changed across the single take: it OPENS under warm desk tungsten (~3200K, distinct amber cast); PARTWAY THROUGH the blinds are opened and cool north-window daylight floods in (~5600K, faint blue, the frame goes slightly brighter and flatter) for the dashboard-talk stretch, with a brief transition beat where both the tungsten and the cool window mix into a split cast; and it CLOSES at golden hour with the low sun raking warm across the walnut desktop (genuinely warm ambience, but the key was still metered so the reference card stays neutral). Slightly flat ungraded contrast straight off the camera throughout, real skin pores and a few stray hair flyaways, faint subtle handheld-feel sway on the locked frame. A neutral 18% grey card and a small white chip are clipped to the desk at the far left edge of frame, IN FRAME for the entire take, as a white-balance reference. The recorded room tone has a low steady air-handler hiss. NO real brand names, logos, screens, or trademarks on any object, screen, product, or clothing — everything plain, unbranded, or fictional only. Candid corporate-explainer look, not CGI-glossy.
inputs.realism_notes: THE SINGLE PRIMARY SOURCE for the whole video lane. It is the media_enhance_speech target (steady room hiss to clean up); it is the ONLY clip video_create_quick_cut shortens — the source is ~210s so the ~90s highlight is a genuine SHORTEN (source > target), never an assembly of multiple clips and never a lengthen; and it is the single source of all six poster frames pulled via video_render_frame. UHD 3840x2160 so pulled frames downscale into the card image frames at >=300 DPI with no upscaling, AND so the 9:16 reframe of the UHD-scale master crops to a ~1215x2160 vertical strip that DOWNSCALES to 1080x1920 (never an upscale). The single take deliberately traverses three lighting STATES (warm tungsten open / cool daylight middle with a mixed transition beat / golden-hour close) so the six frames pulled from different moments carry genuinely different casts and demand non-identical per-frame corrections — the cross-asset grade-match craft, now sourced from ONE clip. The grey card clipped at the desk edge is in frame for the whole take, so every pulled still carries the neutralisation reference. The golden-hour close is the trap: genuinely warm ambience but a metered-neutral card, so its correct grade HOLDS white balance.

inputs.name: norvant_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'NORVANT' wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: a modern geometric sans-serif in deep slate-navy with a small hexring glyph to the left of the word and a single warm-amber accent notch in the glyph. Rendered as a real scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2.5 degrees) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin all around, and the edges are a touch soft as a desktop scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize crisply.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper skew and a fuzzy silhouette if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp/separate the ink from the ground, crop to the mark, knock the off-white to transparency, THEN vectorize. gemini-3-pro-image chosen because the mark carries legible type.

inputs.name: norvant_launchcard.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied, cannot be model-generated): a genuine hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD US Letter (8.5x11) portrait launch card — ONE card per page. It carries live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<card_kind>>, <<line_1>>, <<line_2>>, <<line_3>>, <<accent_label>>, a large image frame wired to an @-prefixed image-path column @frame (for the placed poster frame) and a small corner image frame wired to a second @-prefixed column @logo (for the vector wordmark). Text frames sit in the layout's negative-space zone so the typeset copy reads cleanly over/beside the placed frame. Built by hand so the merge fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid — document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one card's worth of fields and two @-image columns.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd with real <<fields>> plus genuine @-prefixed image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record launch card is the correct connector-doable shape. Two @-image columns (@frame per row, @logo constant) are how the poster frame AND the wordmark both land in the layout; text placement over the image is normal InDesign typesetting, not banned image compositing. A PDF-converted .indd or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.

inputs.name: norvant_launchcard_copy.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied): a 6-row data-merge CSV, one row per launch card, columns exactly matching the template fields: card_kind, line_1, line_2, line_3, accent_label, @frame, @logo. Rows: (1) card_kind='Title', line_1='Norvant', line_2='How your team's busywork runs itself', line_3='A 90-second explainer', accent_label='01', @frame=@hero_title_frame.jpg, @logo=@norvant_wordmark.svg; (2) card_kind='Lower Third', line_1='Maya Ellison', line_2='Founder & Product Lead', line_3='', accent_label='', @frame=@lt_founder_frame.jpg, @logo=@norvant_wordmark.svg; (3) card_kind='Lower Third', line_1='Step 02 - Automate', line_2='What the dashboard does for you', line_3='', accent_label='', @frame=@lt_dashboard_frame.jpg, @logo=@norvant_wordmark.svg; (4) card_kind='Call-out', line_1='3.5 hours', line_2='saved per team, every week', line_3='', accent_label='STAT', @frame=@callout_stat_frame.jpg, @logo=@norvant_wordmark.svg; (5) card_kind='Section', line_1='See it in action', line_2='', line_3='', accent_label='', @frame=@divider_frame.jpg, @logo=@norvant_wordmark.svg; (6) card_kind='End Card', line_1='Start your pilot', line_2='norvant.example / demo', line_3='', accent_label='', @frame=@endcard_frame.jpg, @logo=@norvant_wordmark.svg. All copy is final and must bind verbatim.
inputs.realism_notes: The @frame column is the binding contract: the agent must point each cell at its own produced matched poster frame, and @logo at the produced wordmark.svg, so document_merge_data_layout places imagery AND typesets the client's verbatim copy. Row count = 6 fixes the page=row acceptance gate. Text-only document_merge_data_vector is explicitly the WRONG tool here (it cannot bind the @image columns). No agent copywriting — all card text is supplied.

outputs.name: norvant_master_uhd.mp4
outputs.spec: ~90-second informative explainer/highlight master trimmed DOWN from the single ~3.5-minute UHD interview take (built on the speech-enhanced audio so the dialogue is clean), surfacing the key talking points. Produced by video_create_quick_cut, which SHORTENS the one supplied clip and makes the cut selection itself — the source take (~210s) is longer than the ~90s highlight, so this is a shorten, never an assembly of multiple clips and never a lengthen. Delivered at the source UHD 3840x2160 scale (quick_cut shortens duration, not resolution), H.264. No burned-in captions or motion graphics claimed.

outputs.name: norvant_master_vertical_9x16.mp4
outputs.spec: 9:16 (1080x1920) vertical reframe of the master, SAME length as the master (no trimming), for social teasers. Produced by video_resize as a same-length reframe: the 9:16 crop of the UHD-scale master is a ~1215x2160 vertical strip that DOWNSCALES to 1080x1920 — a legal downscale, never an upscale (this is why the master is retained at UHD scale rather than 1080p).

outputs.name: matched_poster_masters_x6
outputs.spec: Six RETAINED card-bearing neutralised master frames (hero/title, founder lower-third, dashboard lower-third, stat call-out, section divider, golden-hour end card) — the full-frame neutralised grade BEFORE the card-cropping reframe, each still carrying the in-frame 18% grey card and white chip clipped at the desk edge of the take. THESE are the artifacts the grey-card neutrality tolerance is graded on, because the card survives in frame here. All six are pulled from moments of the ONE interview take spanning its three lighting states; each is neutralised to the in-frame grey card and matched to ONE shared house white point and one shared near-black floor (deep, never clipped to 0), with the same lifted-shadow filmic tonality across all six; the hero master additionally carries the masked subject lift that pops the founder off the background without lifting the shared floor. Accompanied by an agent-authored parameter sheet listing, per frame, the white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure move the agent APPLIED (settings it chose by eye, never a measured/recovered value). Acceptance (grader-checked ON THESE card-bearing masters): every grey card reads visually neutral (R,G,B within a tight tolerance) at one shared white point, darks floored at one shared level with no channel crushed to 0, the golden-hour master's warmth preserved (its card held neutral, not cooled), and the per-frame corrections non-identical across the warm vs cool vs mixed frames. sRGB, at the pulled UHD frame resolution (equal to source, never upscaled).

outputs.name: matched_poster_frames_x6
outputs.spec: Six card-ready poster frames — each an off-centre downscale/reframe of its matching card-bearing master (matched_poster_masters_x6) with the far-edge grey/white reference chips cropped OUT, so no card remains in the delivered image. These are the images placed through the merge @frame column. Because the card is cropped away, neutrality is NOT graded on these files — it is graded on the retained masters (card in frame); these simply carry the identical graded look forward from their master. Acceptance (grader-checked): each frame EXCLUDES the reference chips entirely (card-exclusion check), preserves its master's shared house white point / near-black floor / filmic tonality, the hero frame keeps clean negative space on one side for the headline, and each frame is a pure downscale of its UHD-sourced master (never upscaled) sized to fill the card @frame slot at >=300 DPI. sRGB.

outputs.name: norvant_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the NORVANT wordmark (slate-navy type + amber-notched hexring glyph), traced only AFTER the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at card scale with no captured paper ground and no skew.

outputs.name: norvant_launch_cards.pdf
outputs.spec: One press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF of the launch card kit — EXACTLY ONE card per CSV row (page-count = row-count = 6): Title, Founder Lower Third, Dashboard Lower Third, Stat Call-out, Section Divider, End Card — produced by merging norvant_launchcard_copy.csv into the authored single-record norvant_launchcard.indd via document_merge_data_layout, then exported by document_render_layout. Each card binds its <<card_kind>>/<<line_1>>/<<line_2>>/<<line_3>>/<<accent_label>> copy verbatim, places that row's matched poster frame through the @frame column and the vector wordmark through the @logo column. The 'hero' is simply the first page of this merged PDF — there is NO per-record named export. Acceptance gate: card/page count == 6 and each placed frame renders at >=300 DPI at the card image frame (downscale of the UHD-sourced frame). This typeset, image-placed card kit is the owned designed endpoint.

connector_workflow.note: Load the single ~3.5-minute UHD interview take, the wordmark scan, the authored .indd card template and the copy CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream lane has real asset references. Single upload — plumbing, not the difficulty.
Clean the steady room hiss off the interview take's dialogue so the highlight cut has usable audio. [A] async. This is a real dependency: the highlight is built on the cleaned take, not the raw hiss.

Summarise the take to agree the key talking points and a logical flow before cutting, and to decide which moments to pull as poster frames. [A] async. Feeds the cut and the frame-pull decisions; does NOT author any typeset copy (that is client-supplied in the CSV).

Shorten the single ~3.5-minute (~210s) speech-enhanced interview take DOWN to a ~90-second explainer/highlight master, surfacing the key points. video_create_quick_cut only SHORTENS ONE supplied clip and makes the cut selection itself (its creative call, not the agent's) — the source is longer than the target, so nothing is assembled from multiple clips and nothing is lengthened. Resolution is preserved at the source UHD 3840x2160 scale. [A] async. DELIVERABLE.

Reframe the UHD-scale master to 9:16 vertical for social — SAME length, no trimming. The no-stretch 16:9->9:16 crop of the 3840-wide master is a ~1215x2160 vertical strip, which DOWNSCALES to 1080x1920 — a legal downscale, never an upscale (delivering 1080x1920 from a 1080p master would upscale; that is why the master is kept at UHD scale). Consumes the step-4 master. [A] async. DELIVERABLE.

Pull the hero title-card still from a WARM early tungsten moment of the interview take at UHD (3840x2160) — a strong, open moment of the founder to camera with room on one side. [A] async frame-pull from the UHD source take (not the 1080p-equivalent cut) so the placed frame downscales into the card at >=300 DPI. Warm tungsten cast; grey card at desk edge in frame.

Pull the founder lower-third still from another WARM-segment beat of the take at UHD. Same warm tungsten setup as the hero but its own exposure/moment — a per-frame decision, not a copy. Grey card in frame.

Pull the dashboard lower-third still from the COOL daylight segment of the take at UHD (after the blinds were opened), framing the founder leaning to the laptop dashboard. Cool/blue and slightly bright; grey card in frame. Opposite-direction correction from the warm frames.
Pull the stat call-out still from the COOL daylight segment at UHD (a second, tighter beat on the laptop). Cool + bright; grey card in frame.

Pull the section-divider still from the MIXED-light transition beat of the take at UHD (tungsten still on while the cool window is opening), a wider workspace establishing frame. Split warm/cool cast; grey card in frame. Needs a moderate split correction, neither a full warm nor full cool pass.

Pull the end-card still from the GOLDEN-HOUR closing segment of the take at UHD (low sun raking the desk). The scene is genuinely warm but its grey card already reads neutral — this is the trap frame; its grade must HOLD white balance.

ESTABLISH the house look on the hero and record it as the target the other five must hit. Warm tungsten cast: COOL the temperature and set tint to drive the in-frame grey card to true neutral, then build the shared tonality with primitives — floor the darks at the house near-black level (deep, not clipped), roll off highlights to protect skin/window speculars, lift shadows just enough to stay filmic-not-muddy, modest clarity/vibrance. Authored grade, NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone. Report the temp/tint/exposure/black chosen here — they define the common target. [C].
Select the founder subject on the graded hero to drive a selective lift. Semantic subject selection (allowed); returns a mask URI. [C].

Masked selective edit: a small exposure/clarity/vibrance lift on the founder ONLY (using the step-13 mask) so she reads off the background, while the shared black-floor set in step 12 is left untouched. image_apply_adjustments accepts a mask, so this is a genuine local edit — not a whole-image push that would also lift the background and break the house floor. [C].

Honest off-centre crop of the popped UHD hero so the founder sits to one side with clean negative space on the other for the card headline, and the far-edge grey/white reference chips are cropped OUT. Downscale/reframe of existing pixels only — never canvas-extend, never upscale. Sized so it fills the card @frame slot at >=300 DPI. [C]. Feeds the @hero_title_frame cell.

Grade the founder lower-third frame to the SAME target set in step 12. Warm like the hero but its own exposure, so cool the WB to land its grey card on the common white point and set exposure per its own histogram — reported numbers close to the hero's but NOT copied. Match the house floor and tonality. [C].
Crop the reference chips out and resize to the card @frame spec (downscale of UHD, >=300 DPI). [C]. Feeds the @lt_founder_frame cell.

Grade the dashboard lower-third frame — the OPPOSITE-direction correction. Cool/blue and bright, so WARM the WB to neutralise its grey card to the common white point and pull exposure DOWN, then apply the shared floor and tonality so a cool bright moment reads as the same room as the warm ones. Copying the hero's cooling/lifting numbers here is exactly the trap that fails the match. Report its distinct values. [C].
Crop chips out and resize to the card @frame spec (downscale, >=300 DPI). [C]. Feeds the @lt_dashboard_frame cell.

Grade the stat call-out frame to the common target. Cool and bright like the dashboard frame but a different moment/exposure — warm the WB to neutralise its grey card, pull exposure down its own amount, protect any screen/keyboard speculars, seat the shared floor. Its numbers differ again from the dashboard frame's. Report them. [C].
Crop chips out and resize to the card @frame spec (downscale, >=300 DPI). [C]. Feeds the @callout_stat_frame cell.

Grade the section-divider frame to the common target. MIXED cast (warm tungsten + opening cool window), so neither a full warm nor a full cool pass will neutralise the grey card — reason a moderate split temperature/tint to land the card neutral at the shared white point, then match the floor and tonality. A two-bucket 'warm-or-cool' shortcut misses here. Report the move. [C].
Crop chips out and resize to the card @frame spec (downscale, >=300 DPI). [C]. Feeds the @divider_frame cell.

THE TRAP FRAME. The golden-hour close is genuinely warm but was shot under neutral-metered key, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift — only match exposure/brightness and the shared black-floor/tonality to the set. An agent that batch-applies the 'cool the warm frames' logic and cools this one will drive its neutral card off-neutral and strip the golden-hour light the client shot for. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was HELD. [C].

Crop chips out and resize to the card @frame spec, keeping negative space for the end-card CTA (downscale, >=300 DPI). [C]. Feeds the @endcard_frame cell. Frames 1-6 now share one white point and one floor, each neutralised to its own in-frame grey card.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: hero_popped, lt_founder_neutral, lt_dashboard_neutral, callout_stat_neutral, divider_neutral, endcard_neutral
connector_workflow.note: RETAIN the six card-bearing neutralised masters (each still carrying its in-frame grey card and white chip, i.e. the pre-crop grade from steps 14/16/18/20/22/24) as a delivered set. This is the artifact the grey-card neutrality tolerance is graded on, because the placed card frames (steps 15/17/19/21/23/25) have the card cropped OUT and cannot be graded for neutrality. Single retention load — plumbing, not counted as difficulty. [C]. DELIVERABLE.

Prep-before-trace step 1: the wordmark scan sits ~2.5 degrees rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake the rotation into the paths. [C].

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward white so the slate-navy lettering and hexring separate hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges. [C].
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field. [C].

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms and glyph only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). [C].

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the cards. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. [C]. DELIVERABLE.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: hero_title_frame.jpg, lt_founder_frame.jpg, lt_dashboard_frame.jpg, callout_stat_frame.jpg, divider_frame.jpg, endcard_frame.jpg, norvant_wordmark.svg
connector_workflow.note: Bring the six matched poster frames and the vector wordmark into the project so the merge can resolve them by the @frame and @logo columns. Single load — plumbing, not counted as difficulty.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the six copy rows (card_kind/line_1/line_2/line_3/accent_label) into the authored single-record .indd's live <<fields>>, place that row's matched poster frame through the @frame column and the vector wordmark through the @logo column — producing EXACTLY ONE merged card per row (six cards). [T] requires the hand-authored template. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool (text-only, cannot bind the @image columns); a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind; a multi-up grid cannot be produced. This is the connector-correct shape.

Export the merged single-record cards to one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF, one card per row. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all six cards, one per page) in a single call — it cannot export one named card on its own and cannot place an image itself, so the 'hero' is just page 1 (no per-record named export). Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 6; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed. [C]. DELIVERABLE.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) feeds three converging lanes, all sourced from a SINGLE long interview take.
